The architect was José Martin de Aldehuela and the chief builder was Juan Antonio Díaz Machuca.\nThe construction of the newest bridge (the one standing as of 2024) was started in 1759 and took 34 years. There is a chamber above the central arch that was used for a variety of purposes, including as a prison. During the 1936–1939 civil war both sides allegedly used the prison as a torture chamber for captured opponents, killing some by throwing them from the windows to the rocks at the bottom of the El Tajo gorge. The chamber is entered through a square building that was once the guardhouse. It now contains an exhibition describing the bridge's history and construction.\nConstruction of the previous bridge started in 1735; this was the first attempt to span the gorge at this height.
